title: Reduce streaming token latency: token loop refactor, adaptive flush cadence, and backpressure handling
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Streaming token generation latency has been a recurring source of customer complaints and internal perf regressions. Short-lived responses and low-throughput interactive sessions suffer from high tail latency because the token emission loop, batching flush cadence, and backpressure handling were optimized for high throughput rather than per-token latency. This PR introduces a set of complementary changes to reduce end-to-end token emission latency for streaming: 1) refactor the token emitter loop to separate IO flush scheduling from kernel execution, removing blocking flushes from the critical path; 2) adaptive flush cadence: dynamically choose micro-flush intervals based on recent token throughput and client ACK signals; 3) better backpressure handling: non-blocking emission queue with prioritized urgent flushes on client demand and graceful slow-client detection; 4) KV-cache prefetch/warm paths for initial decoding steps to avoid first-token stalls; 5) scheduler/kernels tweak: prefer lightweight kernel paths for very short sequences and prioritize KV-cache hits; 6) telemetry and tests: new latency histogram metrics, deterministic microbench harness, and a perf benchmark entry. Related: builds on fixes in pr-18427*, pr-19642*, pr-20513* and addresses ENG-9876. Checklist:
- [x] Token emitter refactor
- [x] Adaptive flush cadence implementation and config knobs
- [x] Backpressure/queue redesign and tests
- [x] KV cache warm path and microbench
- [x] Kernel selection heuristic change and perf validation
- [x] Integration tests and metrics
Notes: The description includes microbenchmark numbers in the test/bench output. In our internal perf canary runs, median token latency for 1-4 token responses improved ~18-28% (config dependent) and p95 improved ~30-45% in low-throughput scenarios. Full details in the PR comments and perf artifacts.

review_comments: Hiro Tanaka (2026-02-19): Good refactor overall. Two concerns: (1) how does the adaptive cadence behave under highly variable throughput? Please add a short-circuit when observed throughput exceeds X tps so we don't micro-flush excessively; (2) ensure the non-blocking queue has an emergency flush path if the persistent slow client causes queue growth.

Maya Patel (2026-02-19): Responded. Added throughput short-circuit and an emergency_flush trigger when queue length > 1024 or when client signals explicit ack. Added test for emergency flush behavior.
Lina Gomez (2026-02-20): Noted a potential race in KV cache warm path during reentrant calls; requested additional lock-free guards and a unit test for concurrent warm requests.

Maya Patel (2026-02-21): Addressed Lina's comment by switching to atomic state flags and double-checked via the new concurrent warm-path test. Added explanatory comments and microbench results to the PR description.
Arjun Rao (2026-02-22): Approved after CI rerun. Left a note: consider exposing flush_cadence_ms as a per-route knob for Dedicated customers in a follow-up.
CI bot (2026-02-20): integration-tests failed (race in streaming microbench). Reran after fixes (2026-02-21) and all checks passed.
release_notes: Reduced streaming token latency: token emitter refactor, adaptive flush cadence, improved backpressure handling, KV-cache warm path, and kernel selection tweaks. Expected client-visible improvements in short/interactive sessions. Backwards-compatible config knobs added: flush_cadence_ms (default 10ms), emergency_flush_queue_size (default 1024).
